purpose: Everything that must be settled before any NFL line, strategy or reward decision is treated as reasonable, split into what we know, what we do not know, and which suggestion would close each gap.
how_to_read: Q = open question. K = information we actually have with a source. M = information we are missing. S = suggestion, ranked by decision value. Nothing in M is inferred in the site; those cells stay blank.

what_can_be_decided_today: Whether to treat the 32-club standings snapshot and the Week 10 injury listing as adequate scope for a research note (yes, with the stated limits).
Whether the originated Week 10 numbers may be shown as a model exercise (yes, labelled, with no market comparison).
Whether any strategy may be ranked or rewarded (no).
what_cannot_be_decided_today: Whether the originated lines beat, match or lose to the market: no price was retrieved.
Which clubs are relying on second- or third-string players: no published depth chart and no snap counts were retrieved.
Whether the Pythagorean signal has forward predictive value: one partial season, in-snapshot scoring only.
decision_frame.default_recommendation: Publish the research and keep every ranked or paid decision closed until the four blocking items in 'blocking_before_any_reward' are satisfied.

known_information.statement: All 32 clubs have a 2026 record, points for, points against and a displayed win percentage as of the snapshot.
known_information.verification: Parsed from the saved page text; PCT re-derived from W/T/games, NET PTS re-derived from PF minus PA, HOME plus ROAD re-derived to the overall record.

known_information.statement: League scoring level in the snapshot.
known_information.verification: Sum of all PF divided by 272 team-games.

known_information.value: Buffalo 256 PF highest, LA Chargers 121 PF lowest; Jacksonville +108 net highest, LA Chargers -98 lowest
known_information.verification: Maximum and minimum of the parsed PF and NET PTS columns.

known_information.statement: Official injury reporting is mandatory and has fixed categories.
known_information.value: Practice: Did Not Participate / Limited (under 100% of normal reps) / Full (100%). Game status: Out, Doubtful, Questionable. 'Probable' was eliminated.
known_information.verification: Read the NFL news item reporting the Competition Committee revision.

known_information.statement: The Week 10 Thursday listing covers one game only in our snapshot.
known_information.value: 20 players, 9 Commanders and 11 Giants; 2 Out, 1 Questionable, 17 with a blank game status
known_information.verification: Counted from the parsed rows; blanks are copied from the page, not filled.

known_information.statement: Week 10 has 14 fixtures and 4 clubs on bye, covering the league exactly.
known_information.value: 14 fixtures, 28 clubs, plus CHI, DEN, PHI, TB on bye
known_information.verification: Fixture clubs plus byes equal the 32-club standings set; duplicate fixtures rejected.

known_information.statement: Points-based expectation carries real information about the displayed record in this snapshot.
known_information.value: Brier 0.1575 versus 0.25 for a flat .500 guess on 32 clubs
known_information.verification: Same 32 rows scored against the same actual outcomes; p=2.37 taken from the published convention, not fitted.

known_information.statement: Only five of the ten team-level correlations are independent evidence.
known_information.value: Five are structurally induced (net points shares its inputs with PF, PA and wins); no pair exceeds |r| without an arithmetic link.
known_information.verification: Each excluded pair is individually labelled on the correlation page.

known_information.statement: NFL.com terms restrict how this material may be used.
known_information.value: Section 1.3: individual non-commercial informational use only; systematic retrieval to compile a collection, database or directory is prohibited without written consent.
known_information.verification: Read the retrieved terms text, section 1.3.

known_information.statement: The two largest record-versus-scoring gaps are small in absolute terms.
known_information.value: Tampa Bay and Denver are each about 2.17 wins away from expectation; no club is more than 2.2 wins off.
known_information.verification: Actual W plus half of T, minus expected wins, for every club.

missing_information.question: What price, limit and hold does any operator actually offer on these Week 10 markets?
missing_information.why_it_matters: Without a timestamped quote there is no ROI, no closing-line value, no break-even test and no way to rank anything.
missing_information.blocks: Every ranked decision, every reward, all of G06

missing_information.question: Which listed player is a starter, and who replaces him?
missing_information.why_it_matters: The owner requirement names second-, third- and fourth-string exposure. A game status alone cannot tell you whether a starter is out.
missing_information.blocks: Availability-adjusted lines and every player-prop idea

missing_information.question: How many snaps, targets and carries does each player normally take?
missing_information.why_it_matters: Converts an absence into an expected change in team or player output. Without it, 'Out' is a label, not a number.
missing_information.blocks: The injury-to-line adjustment, all player props

missing_information.question: How do same-game legs actually depend on one another?
missing_information.why_it_matters: A parlay price assumes a joint distribution. Multiplying two probabilities assumes zero dependence, which is the assumption this project will not make.

missing_information.question: Is the current snapshot representative of full-season scoring, or is it an eight-game artefact?
missing_information.why_it_matters: Early-season scoring rates are noisy and schedule-dependent; a single partial season cannot support a forward claim.

missing_information.question: Under which operator's rule does each bet settle, especially pushes, overtime and voids?
missing_information.why_it_matters: Two operators can settle the same nominal bet differently, which changes the expected return before any edge is discussed.
missing_information.status: Partly documented for other sports; nothing for NFL

missing_information.question: May this material be published at all in its current form?
missing_information.why_it_matters: NFL.com terms limit use to individual non-commercial informational purposes and prohibit systematic retrieval without consent.
missing_information.blocks: Any dataset release, any commercial use, any redistribution

missing_information.question: What share of the observed record-versus-expectation gap is schedule strength rather than randomness?
missing_information.why_it_matters: The regression idea only becomes a signal once opponent quality is separated from luck.

missing_information.question: What does a blank game status on the official listing mean for that player?
missing_information.why_it_matters: 17 of the 20 listed players have a blank status. Treating blank as 'will play' would be an inference.
missing_information.blocks: Any use of the injury table as a playing-time forecast

missing_information.question: What is the true home-field advantage for these specific fixtures?
missing_information.why_it_matters: We used a single assumed constant of 2.0 points for all 14 games, including an international game in Munich.

suggestions.title: Record one dated operator quote per game, before kickoff
suggestions.problem: M01. No price exists in the record, so nothing can be scored against a market.
suggestions.proposal: For each of the 14 Week 10 games, store the book, market, line, price, limit and the capture timestamp, plus the closing line after kickoff. Two independent captures per game so a transcription error is detectable.
suggestions.effort: Low to moderate; no new analytics, only disciplined capture.
suggestions.unlocks: ROI, closing-line value, break-even comparison, the entire leaderboard.
suggestions.evidence_needed: A quote you are licensed to store, or a public source whose terms permit it.
suggestions.risk_if_skipped: Every performance claim stays permanently unfalsifiable.
suggestions.decision_value: Highest. Nothing else can produce a ranked decision.

suggestions.title: Build a sourced depth-chart and snap-share table
suggestions.problem: M02 and M03. The owner's core requirement about second-, third- and fourth-string players cannot be met by a status label.
suggestions.proposal: Store each club's published depth order by position and each player's recent snap share, then define an absence impact as the difference between the starter's and the replacement's snap-weighted production.
suggestions.effort: Moderate; needs a depth source and per-player usage data.
suggestions.unlocks: Availability-adjusted team lines, position-level vulnerability, honest player-prop work.
suggestions.evidence_needed: A depth chart or roster-order source and official snap counts. Neither was retrieved in this session.
suggestions.risk_if_skipped: The injury page looks thorough while carrying no predictive content.
suggestions.decision_value: High. It converts the owner's stated priority into measurable inputs.

suggestions.title: Measure leg dependence before pricing any parlay
suggestions.problem: M04. A two-leg price needs P(A and B), not P(A) times P(B).
suggestions.proposal: For each candidate leg pair, compute the observed joint hit rate and the phi coefficient on the same games, report a block-bootstrap interval, and refuse to publish a parlay price while the interval spans zero.
suggestions.effort: Moderate; the math is already implemented, the data is not.
suggestions.unlocks: Two-leg pricing, then a defensible three-leg approach with a tested copula or simulation.
suggestions.evidence_needed: Game-level results for both legs on the same dates.
suggestions.risk_if_skipped: Parlay prices look precise and are wrong, which is the most expensive failure mode in this domain.
suggestions.decision_value: High. It is the gate between single bets and every combination product.

suggestions.title: Collect two full prior seasons of game results, then test out of sample
suggestions.problem: M05 and M08. Eight games per club cannot separate skill from schedule or luck.
suggestions.proposal: Store dated final scores for the last two complete seasons, rebuild the scoring projections walk-forward, and score only games that occur after each model's inputs. Compare against both a flat baseline and the originated number.
suggestions.effort: Substantial; it is the largest data task in the list.
suggestions.unlocks: Real out-of-sample scoring, opponent-adjusted ratings, a defensible answer on whether anything is skill-based.
suggestions.evidence_needed: Official dated results you are permitted to store.
suggestions.risk_if_skipped: Every statement stays exploratory and no strategy can ever pass G03.
suggestions.decision_value: High, but it depends on S06 being settled first.

suggestions.title: Write one settlement specification per market before betting it
suggestions.problem: M06. Pushes, overtime, voids and stat corrections decide the result of close bets.
suggestions.proposal: For each market used, record the operator's published settlement rule and re-read it before the first scored bet. Keep a note of every rule discrepancy found between operators.
suggestions.unlocks: Correct scoring of every result, and honest push handling in ROI.
suggestions.evidence_needed: The operator's current published rule text.
suggestions.risk_if_skipped: A winning record can be an artefact of mis-scored pushes.
suggestions.decision_value: Moderate now, essential at the moment a bet is scored.

suggestions.title: Settle the rights question before collecting at scale
suggestions.problem: M07. NFL.com terms restrict systematic retrieval and commercial use.
suggestions.proposal: Keep this as a non-commercial, attributed, frozen research note. Before any bulk or automated collection, obtain written permission or switch to a source whose terms allow it.
suggestions.effort: Low to act on, potentially slow to resolve.
suggestions.unlocks: Any larger dataset, any commercial publication.
suggestions.evidence_needed: Written permission, or a licensed alternative source.
suggestions.risk_if_skipped: The whole research programme rests on a use the publisher prohibits.
suggestions.decision_value: Blocking for scale, not for reading.

suggestions.title: Treat a blank status as unknown and prove it with a test
suggestions.problem: M09. 17 of 20 players have a blank game status.
suggestions.proposal: Keep blank distinct from 'will play' in code and in the interface, and add a test that fails if a blank is ever converted into an implied availability.
suggestions.unlocks: Protects every downstream claim from a silent inference.
suggestions.evidence_needed: None beyond the interface and test.
suggestions.risk_if_skipped: The site would quietly assert that most listed players are available.
suggestions.decision_value: Moderate; cheap insurance against the most likely hallucination in this dataset.
suggestions.status: Proposed · partially in place (blanks are already kept blank)

suggestions.title: Replace the single home-field constant with a tested range
suggestions.problem: M10. One assumed 2.0-point constant is applied to every game, including a neutral-site international fixture.
suggestions.proposal: Run the originated lines across a plausible range of home adjustments and publish the range alongside the point estimate. Flag the Munich game as a neutral-site case rather than a home game.
suggestions.unlocks: Honest uncertainty on every spread, and one fewer hidden assumption.
suggestions.evidence_needed: None to start; a sourced value would be better than a range.
suggestions.risk_if_skipped: A single arbitrary number drives every spread on the site.
suggestions.decision_value: Moderate. It improves honesty more than accuracy.

suggestions.title: Publish the shadow ledger now, empty, with its rules locked
suggestions.problem: No forward record exists, so no reward can ever be earned.
suggestions.proposal: Freeze the entry format, scoring rule and stake cap before the first entry, and never edit a row after settlement.
suggestions.unlocks: A reward process that cannot be gamed after the fact.
suggestions.risk_if_skipped: Rewards, when they eventually appear, will be judged on hindsight.
suggestions.decision_value: Moderate; it is what makes the leaderboard credible later.
suggestions.status: Published empty on the leaderboard page

suggestions.title: Add a two-source rule for every future value
suggestions.problem: Every value on this site currently rests on one retrieved page.
suggestions.proposal: Require a second independent official confirmation for any value used in a decision, and mark everything else as single-source.
suggestions.unlocks: Detection of transcription and rendering errors before they reach a decision.
suggestions.evidence_needed: A genuinely independent source, not a mirror of the same feed.
suggestions.risk_if_skipped: A rendering quirk becomes a permanent 'fact'.
suggestions.decision_value: Moderate. One source is enough to read a page; two are needed to trust a number.
suggestions.status: Proposed · current values are single-source and labelled as such

sequence: S06 rights check (cheap, prevents wasted work)
S02 depth and snaps (unblocks the owner's availability requirement)
S05 settlement rules, S07 blank discipline, S08 home-field range (hygiene)
S09 ledger, S10 second source (long-run credibility)
acceptance_tests: A proposed change must name the question it closes and the file that will hold the new evidence.
No cell may move from blank to a value without an official URL and a check date.
A strategy may only leave the blocked state when every applicable gate cites an artifact URL.
The site must rebuild byte-identically after the change, with no broken links.
An option that adds a number but no verification must be rejected.
